title: He wasn’t lost.
paragraphs: That’s the tension in Gospel of Luke 2.
A twelve-year-old boy stands in the temple—dust in the air, ancient stone walls breathing history, scholars leaning in… listening.
Because while heaven was speaking in the temple, His parents were searching in the crowd.
Mary’s chest tight. Joseph scanning faces. Every shadow a disappointment.
Sitting among teachers. Asking questions that pierced. Answering with wisdom that silenced grown men.
And then comes the line that slices through human expectation:
“Did you not know that I must be about My Father’s business?” — Luke 2:49 (NKJV)

Who He was.
Whose He was.
Why He came.
You can walk with Jesus for years… and still lose sight of Him.
Mary and Joseph didn’t abandon Him.
How many of us are moving forward in life—career, relationships, ministry, dreams—thinking Jesus is “somewhere in the group”… while our direction has quietly drifted away from the Father’s will?
But we haven’t actually checked if He’s with us.
Because even when they misunderstood Him…
Scripture says He went down with them and was subject to them (Luke 2:51).
The Son of God—perfect, pure, fully aware of His divine identity—chose submission.
He didn’t use His identity to rebel.
And that points us somewhere deeper.
This moment in the temple is not just a childhood story.
The same Jesus who said, “I must be about My Father’s business” would later walk straight into a cross.
Because the Father’s business… was you.

Your sin.
Your wandering.
Your quiet compromises.
Your hidden guilt.
Your double life.
Your religious mask.
The boy in the temple became the Lamb on the hill.
And on that cross, Jesus didn’t just answer questions…
He answered the problem of your soul.
No amount of effort, morality, or religion could close that gap.
But Jesus lived the life you couldn’t live—perfect, obedient, surrendered.
Then He died the death you deserved.
So that lost people could be found.
Let me speak straight to your heart.
Some of you are like Mary and Joseph right now.
Maybe even feel like you’ve lost God.
Go back to where you last truly encountered Him.
Not the version of faith you perform online.

Where Scripture is open.
Where your heart is honest.
Where surrender is not theoretical.
Jesus is not hiding from you.
But He will not compete with everything else you keep choosing over Him.
He has always been about the Father’s business.
Because the same Jesus in Luke 2…
Say it in your heart right now:
“Jesus, bring me back to the Father.”
